58. The correct set that contains all kinds (basic, acidic, amphoteric and neutral) of oxides is :

59. Given below are two statements :

Statement-II : The correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy is $\mathrm{Si}<\mathrm{Ge}<\mathrm{Pb}<\mathrm{Sn}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
(1) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
(2) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
(3) Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
(4) Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

Ans. (2)

$$\underset{(2427 \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol})}{\mathbf{B}}>\underset{(1979 \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol})}{\mathbf{G a}^{-}}>\underset{(1816 \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol})}{\mathbf{A l}}$$

Order of I ionization energy for carbon family elements is :
$$\underset{(786 \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol})}{\mathrm{Si}}>\underset{(761 \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol})}{\mathrm{Ge}}>\underset{(715 \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol})}{\mathrm{Pb}}>\underset{(708 \mathrm{KJ} / \mathrm{mol})}{\mathrm{Sn}}$$

61. Which of the following complexes will show coordination isomerism ?
(A) $\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_{2}\right]$
(B) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]$
(C) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]$
(D) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]$
(E) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(1) B, C and D Only
(2) B, D and E Only
(3) A, C and D Only
(4) C, D and E Only

Ans. (1, 2, 4)
Sol. Compound, $\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_{2}\right]$ cannot show coordination isomerism. All other complexes (B, C, D and E) will show co-ordination isomerism.

62. Complete combustion of Xg of an organic compound gave 0.25 g of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and 0.12 g of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$. If the \% of carbon is 25\% and of hydrogen is $4.89 \%$, then $\mathrm{X}=$ $\_\_\_\_$ $\times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~g}$. (Nearest integer) (Molar mass of C, H and O are 12, 1 and $16 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively.)
(1) 273
(2) 27
(3) 2730
(4) 227

Ans. (1)
Sol. Mass of carbon $=\frac{0.25}{44} \times 12$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { Mass } \% \text { of carbon }=\frac{\text { Mass of carbon }}{\mathrm{x}} \times 100 \\
\mathrm{x}=\frac{\frac{0.25 \times 12}{44} \times 100}{25} \\
\mathrm{x}=\frac{12}{44} \\
\mathrm{x}=0.2727=272.7 \times 10^{-3} \\
\simeq 273 \times 10^{-3}
\end{array}$$

71. The surface of sodium metal is irradiated with radiation of wavelength x nm. The kinetic energy of ejected electrons is $2.8 \times 10^{-20} \mathrm{~J}$. The work function of sodium is 2.3 eV . The value of x is
$\_\_\_\_$ $\times 10^{2} \mathrm{~nm}$. (Nearest integer) (Given : $\mathrm{h}=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~s} ; 1 \mathrm{eV}=1.60 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J}$; $\mathrm{c}=3.0 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ )
Ans. (5)

Sol. for photoelectric effect :
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}=\mathrm{W}+\text { K.E. } \\
\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^{8}}{\mathrm{x}}=2.3 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}+2.8 \times 10^{-20} \\
\frac{19.8 \times 10^{-26}}{\mathrm{x}}=3.96 \times 10^{-19} \\
\mathrm{x}=5 \times 10^{-7} \\
\mathrm{x}=500 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~m} \\
\mathrm{x}=5 \times 10^{2} \mathrm{~nm}
\end{array}$$
72. Consider the following gas phase reaction being carried out in a closed vessel at 25°C.
$$2 \mathrm{~A}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{~B}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{~g})$$

\begin{tabular}[t]{|l|l|}
\hline $\frac{\text { time }}{\text { (min) }}$ & total pressure of the $\frac{\text { system }}{(\mathrm{mm} \mathrm{Hg})}$ \\
\hline 30 & 300 \\
\hline $\infty$ & 600 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

The pressure of $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$ at 30 minutes time interval would be $\_\_\_\_$ mm Hg. (Nearest integer)

Ans. (20)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\quad 2 A(g) \rightarrow 4 B(g)+C(g) \\
\quad p^{\circ} \\
t=30 \min \quad p^{\circ}-2 x \quad 4 x \quad x \\
t=\infty \quad-\quad 2 p^{\circ} \quad p^{\circ} / 2 \\
p_{\infty}=2 p^{\circ}+p^{\circ} / 2=600 \\
5 p^{\circ} / 2=600 \\
P^{\circ}=240 \mathrm{~mm} \mathrm{Hg} \\
\text { At } \mathrm{t}=30 \mathrm{~min}, \mathrm{p}=300=p^{\circ}-2 x+4 x+x \\
300=240+3 x \\
3 x=60 \\
x=20
\end{array}$$

Pressure of $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})=20 \mathrm{~mm} \mathrm{Hg}$

73. Consider the following two half-cell reactions along with the standard reduction potential given :
$$\begin{array}{ll}
\mathrm{CO}_{2}+6 \mathrm{H}^{+}+6 \mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} & \mathrm{E}_{\text {red }}^{\mathrm{o}}=0.02 \mathrm{~V} \\
\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}+2 \mathrm{H}^{+}+2 \mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} & \mathrm{E}_{\text {red }}^{\mathrm{o}}=1.23 \mathrm{~V}
\end{array}$$

The fuel cell was set up using the above two reactions such that the cell operates under the standard condition of 1 bar pressure and 298 K temperature. The fuel cell works with 80\% efficiency. If the work derived from the cell using 1 mol of $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}$ is used to compress an ideal gas isothermally against a constant pressure of 1kPa, then the change in the volume of the gas, $\Delta \mathrm{V}=$ $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m}^{3}$. (Nearest integer)
Given : $\mathrm{F}=96500 \mathrm{C} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$
Ans. (560)
Sol. $\mathrm{E}_{\text {cell }}^{\circ}=[1.23-0.02]=1.21 \mathrm{~V}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=-6 \times 96500 \times 1.21 \mathrm{~J} \\
\mathrm{~W}=\frac{80}{100} \times \Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=-\mathrm{P} \Delta \mathrm{~V} \\
0.8 \times 6 \times 96500 \times 1.21=1 \times 10^{3}(\Delta \mathrm{~V}) \\
\Delta \mathrm{V}=560.472 \mathrm{~m}^{3}
\end{array}$$

(2) 2020
(3) 2000
(4) 1000

Ans. (2)
Sol. $\quad(\text { W.D. })_{\mathrm{g}}+(\text { W.D. })_{\text {sand }}=\Delta \mathrm{K}$

37. An electromagnetic wave travels in free space along the $x$-direction. At a particular point in space and time, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}=2 \times 10^{-7} \hat{\mathrm{j}} \mathrm{T}$ is associated with this wave. 40. Two point charges $8 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $-2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are located at $\mathrm{x}=2 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $\mathrm{x}=4 \mathrm{~cm}$, respectively on the x -axis. The ratio of electric flux due to these charges through two spheres of radii 3 cm and 5 cm with their centers at the origin is $\_\_\_\_$ .
(1) $4: 1$
(2) 3 : 4
(3) 4 : 3
$(4) 4: 5$
Ans. (3)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
x=0 & \mathrm{q}_{1}=8 \mu \mathrm{C} & \mathrm{q}_{2}=-2 \mu \mathrm{C} \\
{ }_{\mathrm{x}}=2 & \mathrm{x}=4
\end{array}$$

For sphere with radius 3 cm and center origin
$$\phi_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{en}}}{\varepsilon_{0}}=\frac{8 \mu \mathrm{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}}$$
for sphere of radius 5 cm
$$\begin{aligned}
\phi_{2} & =\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{en}}}{\varepsilon_{0}}=\frac{(8-2) \mu \mathrm{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}}=\frac{6 \mu \mathrm{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}} \\
\frac{\phi_{1}}{\phi_{2}} & =\frac{8}{6}=\frac{4}{3}=1.33 \\
\frac{\phi_{1}}{\phi_{2}} & =1.33
\end{aligned}$$
